⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Asymptotic Analysis

Consider the recurrence relation: $T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n / \log_2 n$ for $n > 1$ with $T(1) = 1$. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Here $a=2, b=2, f(n)=n/\log n$. $n^{\log_b a} = n^1 = n$. The ratio $\frac{n^{\log_b a}}{f(n)} = \log n$ is asymptotically positive but not polynomially larger ($n^\epsilon$). Thus Master theorem Case 1 does not apply. By substitution $n=2^k$: $T(2^k) = 2T(2^{k-1}) + 2^k/k$. Dividing by $2^k$: $\frac{T(2^k)}{2^k} = \frac{T(2^{k-1})}{2^{k-1}} + \frac{1}{k}$. Let $S(k) = \frac{T(2^k)}{2^k}$, then $S(k) = \sum_{i=1}^k 1/i = \ln k = \Theta(\log k) = \Theta(\log(\log n))$. Thus $T(n) = \Theta(n \log(\log n))$.

questions.questionHtml:
⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Sorting

What is the minimum number of comparisons required to determine both the minimum and maximum elements in an unsorted array of size 100 using an optimal pairwise comparison algorithm?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
For an array of $n$ elements, comparing elements in pairs takes $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ comparisons. The winners compete for maximum ($\lceil n/2 ceil - 1$ comparisons) and the losers compete for minimum ($\lceil n/2 ceil - 1$ comparisons). Total $= \lceil 3n/2 \rceil - 2$. For $n=100$: $3(100)/2 - 2 = 150 - 2 = 148$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Greedy Algorithms

Consider the Fractional Knapsack problem with items having values $v_i$ and weights $w_i$. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
A is TRUE: Standard greedy algorithm on $v_i/w_i$ is optimal for fractional knapsack.
B is FALSE: 0/1 knapsack requires dynamic programming; greedy heuristic fails.
C is TRUE: Since every unit of weight yields identical value, any combination reaching full capacity achieves max value.
D is TRUE: Using median-of-medians $O(n)$ selection to find the pivot ratio and partitioning achieves $O(n)$ without full sorting.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Graph Algorithms

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a directed graph. Which of the following conditions is both necessary and sufficient for $G$ to have a topological sorting?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
A topological sort exists if and only if the directed graph contains no directed cycles (i.e., it is a Directed Acyclic Graph, DAG). Strongly connected graphs with $>1$ vertices contain cycles and have no topological ordering.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Divide and Conquer

Standard matrix multiplication of two $2 \times 2$ matrices requires 8 scalar multiplications. Strassen's algorithm reduces the number of scalar multiplications of $2 \times 2$ block matrices to:

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Strassen's algorithm uses 7 multiplications instead of 8, leading to recurrence $T(n) = 7T(n/2) + O(n^2)$, giving complexity $O(n^{\log_2 7}) \approx O(n^{2.807})$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Dynamic Programming

Consider two sequences $X = \langle A, B, C, B, D, A, B \rangle$ and $Y = \langle B, D, C, A, B, A \rangle$. What is the length of the Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) of $X$ and $Y$?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Common subsequences include $\langle B, C, B, A \rangle$, $\langle B, D, A, B \rangle$, and $\langle B, C, A, B \rangle$. Each has length 4. There is no common subsequence of length 5.

questions.questionHtml:
⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Graph Algorithms

Consider a directed graph $G = (V, E)$ with $|V| = 12$ and $|E| = 45$. In the worst-case, how many total edge relaxation operations are performed by the Bellman-Ford algorithm to compute single-source shortest paths (excluding negative cycle detection pass)?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Bellman-Ford runs $|V|-1$ passes over all $|E|$ edges. Total edge relaxations $= (|V| - 1) \times |E| = (12 - 1) \times 45 = 11 \times 45 = 495$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Minimum Spanning Tree

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a connected, weighted graph with distinct edge weights. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
A is TRUE: Prim grows a single tree vertex by vertex.
B is TRUE: Kruskal picks lightest non-cycle edges anywhere in the graph, forming a forest.
C is TRUE: Sorting takes $O(|E| \log |E|) = O(|E| \log |V|)$, and union-find takes $O(|E| \alpha(|V|))$.
D is TRUE: With distinct weights, the lightest edge is always chosen; the second lightest cannot create a cycle with only one edge, so it is always picked in Kruskal's second step.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | NP-Completeness

Let $L_1, L_2$ be two decision problems. Suppose $L_1 \le_P L_2$ (i.e. $L_1$ is polynomial-time reducible to $L_2$). Which of the following deductions is GUARANTEED TO BE VALID?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Reducibility $L_1 \le_P L_2$ means $L_2$ is at least as hard as $L_1$. If the harder problem $L_2$ can be solved in polynomial time ($L_2 \in P$), then the easier problem $L_1$ can also be solved in polynomial time by reducing it in poly-time to $L_2$ and solving it.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Divide and Conquer

Consider the recurrence relation $T(n) = 3T(n/3) + n$ with $T(1) = 2$. What is the exact value of $T(27)$?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
$T(1) = 2$.
$T(3) = 3T(1) + 3 = 3(2) + 3 = 9$.
$T(9) = 3T(3) + 9 = 3(9) + 9 = 36$.
$T(27) = 3T(9) + 27 = 3(36) + 27 = 108 + 27 = 135$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Graph Algorithms

In the Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path algorithm on an $n$-vertex graph, what does entry $D^{(k)}[i][j]$ represent after the $k$-th iteration?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Floyd-Warshall is parameterized by the set of allowed intermediate vertices: $D^{(k)}[i][j] = \min(D^{(k-1)}[i][j], D^{(k-1)}[i][k] + D^{(k-1)}[k][j])$, meaning intermediate vertices are strictly drawn from $\{1, 2, \dots, k\}$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Greedy Algorithms

Consider 6 intervals with [start, end] times: $[1, 4], [3, 5], [0, 6], [5, 7], [3, 9], [5, 9], [6, 10], [8, 11]$. What is the maximum number of mutually compatible (non-overlapping) intervals that can be selected?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
Greedy choice by earliest finish time:
1. Pick $[1, 4]$ (finishes at 4).
2. Compatible remaining: $[5, 7], [5, 9], [6, 10], [8, 11]$. Earliest finish is $[5, 7]$ (finishes at 7).
3. Compatible remaining: $[8, 11]$. Pick $[8, 11]$.
Total compatible intervals = 3 ($\{[1,4], [5,7], [8,11]\}$).

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Sorting

For an array of $n = 63$ distinct elements, in the ideal best-case scenario where QuickSort always partitions arrays into two equal halves of size $(n-1)/2$, what is the total depth of the recursion tree (counting root as level 0)?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
At level 0: 63 elements.
Level 1: 31 elements.
Level 2: 15 elements.
Level 3: 7 elements.
Level 4: 3 elements.
Level 5: 1 element.
Tree depth (with root = level 0) $= \log_2(63 + 1) - 1 = 6 - 1 = 5$.

⚡ GO Classes CS 2027 Style | Algorithms - Backtracking

In the 4-Queens problem solved using backtracking on a $4 \times 4$ chessboard, how many distinct valid non-attacking configurations exist?

💡 Official Solution & Step-by-Step Derivation:
The 4-Queens problem has exactly 2 distinct solutions: [2, 4, 1, 3] and [3, 1, 4, 2] (1-indexed column positions for rows 1 to 4), which are mirror reflections of each other.
